items.title: Jimmy Wormworth interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002
items.q: I got to the point when I was about 11 where I had a lot of the passages memorized, Art Tatum passages and whole Nat Cole records, each record memorized

ctx.x: Uh, in 1946 around January, not long after Christmas, one of my uncles who was stationed in the Pacific in World War II came home and with some of the money he had saved from his allotment, which he sent to my grandmother, not long after he got home he was influenced by probably my Uncle Dick and maybe my aunts, to buy a record player, well what in those days was called a combination. It’s a console record player and radio, when there was still 78s. It was the latest thing. Zenith. And so he bought this record…

that’s why he was such a good singer. He had a good instrument, good vocal chords and such knowledge. So those records and those Art Tatum records just took me off in the whole direction of music. I used to beg — I was spoiled rotten — and I’d beg my mother and my aunts, “Oh I don’t feel good, could I stay home from school?” “All right honey, what’s wrong?” And I’d stay home and all I would do is play those records over and over, and play passages.
